profile_text.body:
Cerence Inc. describes itself as delivering conversational and agentic AI-powered user experiences for automotive and beyond, under the tagline "AI for a World in Motion." The company says its CaLLM family of language models brings conversational AI to the automotive world and beyond, enabling natural, multimodal, and safe interactions. Its site also discusses AI for automotive dealerships, industrial AI with multimodal perception and voice interaction, and scalable embedded in-car AI platforms for North American OEMs.

The company's Cerence Emergency Vehicle Detection (EVD) product uses Audio AI to detect emergency vehicles and alert ADAS and autonomous driving systems. According to the site, EVD is deployed in production vehicles, can detect more than 1,500 emergency sirens across nearly 50 countries, and can identify approaching emergency vehicles from more than 300 meters away with interior microphones and beyond 800 meters with exterior microphones. Cerence reported third quarter results with revenue up 12% YoY, connected services revenue up 20% YoY, and operating cash flow of $20M supporting a first-ever share repurchase program. The site also describes work with Microsoft on Zero Trust and layered AI security for in-car assistants.

Cerence Inc. is a for-profit public company headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts, with ticker CRNC and CIK 0001768267. It has 191 Massachusetts law exposure entries and no recorded litigation cases.
